data.title: Semiconductors will rally by the end of the year, says SA analyst
data.description:
Semiconductors should be headed towards positive territory into the end of the year, said Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research.

While semiconductors , ended higher this week, the group saw big losses this week amid a continued technology selloff due to fears around elevated AI expenditures.

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF ended up 0.7% on Friday but lost 4.56% this week. Similarly, the iShares Semiconductor ETF closed up 0.5% but declined almost 6% this week.

“I think semiconductors and everything else is headed up into year-end. Possibly without those who were shaken out this week,” King said.

On the other hand, the Dow ended higher this week, adding 0.4% to weekly gains, even when the index lost 1.2% on Friday.

Small caps also saw a week of gains, as well as defense stocks , , U.S. government bonds , , , and even biotech , , King noted.

Bitcoin declined 0.6% in the past five days and was flat on Friday.

“The crypto boogeyman was flat. Despite which there is a caterwaul of crying in the casino, which can only be because people are far too concentrated in the same high-beta semiconductor and component stocks,” King said.

data.title: Aberdeen Multi-Market Income Fund announces 1-for-4 reverse stock split
data.description:
Key points:

  • Aberdeen Multi-Market Income Fund said on Friday that its board approved a 1-for-4 reverse stock split of the fund's issued and outstanding common shares, effective November 9, 2026.

  • The board approved the reverse stock split to increase the fund's per-share market price that could help reduce certain trading and administrative frictions associated with lower-priced securities, increase the fund's suitability for certain investment platforms and intermediary programs, and better align the fund's share price with industry trading conventions, the company said.

  • No fractional shares will be issued.

data.title: IC Group Holdings Inc. Announces Leadership Realignment to Support Strategic Priorities and Related Restructuring Charge
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 23, 2026) - IC Group Holdings Inc. ("IC Group" or "the Company"), a consumer engagement company driving commerce and data for global brands and professional sports teams today announced a leadership realignment designed to strengthen execution against its strategic priorities, improve organizational efficiency and support the Company's next phase of growth.

As part of this realignment, Marc Caron, Chief Operating Officer, will be departing from the Company and has resigned as a Director. In addition, other non-officer positions have been eliminated. The changes are effective immediately.

"As IC Group enters its next phase of growth, we are aligning our leadership structure to sharpen execution and deliver sustainable, long-term value," said Duncan McCready, Chief Executive Officer. "These changes are intended to simplify decision-making, enhance accountability, improve cross-functional alignment and ensure our resources are focused on the areas that will drive the greatest value for customers, employees and shareholders. We are grateful to Marc and all affected team members for their contributions and dedication to IC Group and wish them continued success."

As a result of these decisions, the Company expects to record a restructuring charge of approximately $1.0 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, consisting primarily of severance and related employee transition costs. Annual savings from the elimination of these positions are estimated to be approximately $900,000. The restructuring charge is expected to be paid over the next 14 months.

About IC Group

IC Group is a consumer engagement company driving commerce and data for global brands and professional sports teams across live events, digital ecosystems, and mobile channels. Operating at the intersection of marketing, technology, and commerce, we simplify the complexities of modern consumer engagement for customers on a global scale.

data.title: First Capital, Inc. Reports Quarterly Earnings
data.description:
CORYDON, Ind., Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- First Capital, Inc. (the “Company”) , the holding company for First Harrison Bank (the “Bank”), today reported net income of $5.1 million, or $1.53 per diluted share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $4.5 million, or $1.34 per diluted share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

Results of Operations for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 and 2025

Net interest income after provision for credit losses increased $1.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Interest income increased $1.4 million when comparing the two periods due to an increase in the average tax-equivalent yield(1) on interest-earning assets from 4.94% for the third quarter of 2025 to 5.23% for the same period in 2026, in addition to an increase in the average balance of interest-earning assets from $1.20 billion for the third quarter of 2025 to $1.25 billion for the same period in 2026. Interest expense decreased $119,000 when comparing the periods as the average cost of interest-bearing liabilities decreased from 1.66% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to 1.57% for the same period in 2026 while the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities increased from $891.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to $911.5 million for the same period in 2026. As a result of the changes in interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, the tax-equivalent net interest margin(1) increased from 3.71% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to 4.08% for the same period in 2026. Refer to the accompanying average balance sheet for more information regarding changes in the composition of the Company’s balance sheet and resulting yields and costs from the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Based on management’s analysis of the Allowance for Credit Losses (“ACL”) on loans and unfunded loan commitments, the provision for credit losses increased from $150,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 to $355,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Bank recognized net charge-offs of $123,000 and $17,000 for the quarters ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Noninterest income decreased $14,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The decrease is primarily due to the Company recognizing a $9,000 loss on equity securities during the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to a gain of $150,000 during the same period in 2025. That decrease was partially offset by the Company recognizing increases of $92,000 and $57,000 in other income and service charges on deposit accounts, respectively, when comparing the two periods. The increase in other income was primarily due to the Company recognizing $48,000 and $45,000 in income from its technology investment fund and its renewable energy tax credit investment, respectively, during the quarter.

Noninterest expenses increased $545,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. This was primarily due to increases in compensation and benefits and other expenses of $585,000 and $75,000, respectively, when comparing the two periods. The increase in compensation and benefits is due to increases in salary and wages associated with annual cost of living and performance related adjustments as well as increases in the cost of Company-provided health insurance benefits. The increase in other expenses was primarily due to general inflationary pressures and routine pricing increases rather than any specific item. These increases were partially offset by a $148,000 decrease in occupancy and equipment expenses when comparing the two periods. Occupancy and equipment expenses were elevated during the third quarter of 2025 due to disposal losses associated with two of the Bank’s branches, the upgrade of the Company’s call center system, and the demolition of one of the Bank’s branches. None of these were present during the third quarter of 2026.

Income tax expense increased $164,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025 resulting in an effective tax rate of 19.4% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to 19.2% for the same period in 2025.

Results of Operations for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 and 2025

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $14.2 million, or $4.25 per diluted share, compared to net income of $11.5 million, or $3.43 per diluted share, for the same period in 2025.

Net interest income after provision for credit losses increased $4.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Interest income increased $4.6 million when comparing the two periods due to an increase in the average tax-equivalent yield(1) on interest-earning assets from 4.80% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to 5.10% for the same period in 2026, in addition to an increase in the average balance of interest-earning assets from $1.19 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $1.24 billion for the same period in 2026. Interest expense decreased $471,000 when comparing the periods as the average cost of interest-bearing liabilities decreased from 1.67% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to 1.56% for the same period in 2026 while the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities increased from $886.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $906.8 million for the same period in 2026. As a result of the changes in interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, the tax-equivalent net interest margin(1) increased from 3.55% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to 3.96% for the same period in 2026. Refer to the accompanying average balance sheet for more information regarding changes in the composition of the Company’s balance sheet and resulting yields and costs from the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Based on management’s analysis of the ACL on loans and unfunded loan commitments, the provision for credit losses increased from $794,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $1.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The Bank recognized net charge-offs of $292,000 and $214,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Noninterest income increased $373,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase is primarily due to the Company recognizing a $261,000 gain on equity securities during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to a gain of $127,000 during the same period in 2025. In addition, the Company recognized increases of $110,000, $70,000 and $50,000 in service charges on deposit accounts, other income and ATM and debit card fee income, respectively, when comparing the two periods. The increase in other income was primarily due to the Company recognizing a $47,000 increase in income from its renewable energy tax credit investment during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, in addition to $48,000 of income from its technology investment fund during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 that the Company did not receive during the same period in 2025. These were partially offset by the Company recognizing a $47,000 gain on the redemption of a bank-owned life insurance policy during the nine months ended September 30, 2025, and no such redemption occurred during the same period in 2026.

Noninterest expenses increased $1.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. This was primarily due to increases in compensation and benefits, other expenses, professional services, and advertising expenses of $1.1 million, $253,000, $132,000 and $92,000, respectively, when comparing the two periods. The increase in compensation and benefits is due to increases in salary and wages associated with annual cost of living and performance related adjustments as well as increases in the cost of Company-provided health insurance benefits. The increase in other expenses is primarily due to a $70,000 increase in consumer fraud losses and general inflationary pressures and routine pricing increases during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. The increase in professional services is due to increased consulting fees. The increase in advertising expenses is related to various new marketing campaigns undertaken during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. These increases were partially offset by a decrease in occupancy and equipment expenses of $110,000 due to a reduction in building maintenance expenses.

Income tax expense increased $919,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025 resulting in an effective tax rate of 19.8% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 18.4% for the same period in 2025. The increase in the Company’s effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 reflects a higher proportion of net income being subject to taxation compared to the same period last year.

Comparison of Financial Condition at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025

Total assets were $1.27 billion at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025. Net loans receivable and other assets increased $20.9 million and $2.2 million, respectively, from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026. These increases were partially offset by a decrease of $22.5 million in available for sale securities when comparing the two periods. Deposits increased $6.4 million from $1.12 billion at December 31, 2025 to $1.13 billion at September 30, 2026. Nonperforming assets (consisting of nonaccrual loans, accruing loans 90 days or more past due, and foreclosed real estate) increased from $4.4 million at December 31, 2025 to $5.5 million at September 30, 2026. The increase was primarily due to the nonaccrual classification of a non-owner occupied commercial real estate loan.

The Bank currently has 17 offices in the Indiana communities of Corydon, Edwardsville, Greenville, Floyds Knobs, Palmyra, New Albany, New Salisbury, Jeffersonville, Salem, Lanesville and Charlestown and the Kentucky communities of Shepherdsville, Mt. Washington and Lebanon Junction.

Access to First Harrison Bank accounts, including online banking and electronic bill payments, is available through the Bank’s website at www.firstharrison.com. For more information and financial data about the Company, please visit Investor Relations at the Bank’s aforementioned website. The Bank can also be followed on Facebook.

data.title: Honda and Mitsubishi Motors Sign First-ever MOU on Complementary Automobile Product Supply
data.description:
TOKYO, Japan, Oct 23, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Honda Motor Co., Ltd. (Honda) and Mitsubishi Motors Corporation (Mitsubishi Motors) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) for the development of a Honda model based on the Mitsubishi Triton pickup truck. This marks the first initiative between the two companies for complementary supply to each other's product lineups. The new Honda model is scheduled to go on sale in the ASEAN market in 2028.

Honda and Mitsubishi Motors have been exploring opportunities for collaboration in various areas based on the framework of the strategic partnership which was part of an MOU signed on August 1, 2024, among three companies, including Nissan Motor Co., Ltd.

One of the opportunities the three companies have been extensively exploring and discussing from both short- and medium-to-long-term perspectives is the complementary supply of each other's vehicles. This would enable the three companies to leverage each other's globally competitive automobile products to quickly and efficiently enhance their respective product lineups aligned to the business environment and customer needs of each company in different regions.

The Mitsubishi Triton, which is the subject of this complementary vehicle supply arrangement, is a one-ton pickup truck built on a robust ladder frame. It is one of Mitsubishi Motors' global strategic models that is in high demand, particularly in the ASEAN region.

Through this collaboration, Honda will add a pickup truck model to its lineup primarily in the ASEAN market, where it does not currently offer pickup truck models, enabling Honda to enhance its product lineup quickly and efficiently in the market. Meanwhile, this collaboration will enable Mitsubishi Motors to increase production volume and improve capacity utilization at its production plant in Thailand. The two companies reached this agreement after determining that this collaboration would generate synergies for both companies.

Going forward, the three companies will continue to deepen their strategic partnership to further strengthen their competitiveness and ability to meet diverse customer needs while fully utilizing their respective products and technological assets.

Source: Honda Motor Co, Ltd

data.title: Moderna, Meta, SpaceX, Bloom Energy, AT&T, and More Stocks That Explain Today's Market — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Callum Keown and Mariapaula Gonzalez

Stocks traded mixed Friday as oil prices rose, while some of the hard-hit tech names slightly rebounded following a brutal selloff in the previous session.

Moderna was up 1.1% after an 18% slump Thursday following a data leak for the cancer vaccine candidate the drugmaker is developing with Merck.

Telecom giants AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile were all down following a report that SpaceX was in talks to secure 80,000 cell towers as it looks to challenge the wireless carriers. Cell tower owners Crown Castle and American Tower jumped 9.8% and 3.8% respectively. Meanwhile, SpaceX rose 1.7%.

Bloom Energy slumped 12%. While the energy technology company raised its full-year 2026 earnings-per-share guidance, it reported negative free cash flow for the third quarter.

Deckers Outdoor fell 4.7% after the Ugg maker cut its revenue outlook when it reported earnings late Thursday.

American Express declined 4.2%. The company said Friday it would cut 5% of its global jobs. On top of that, its revenue for the fiscal third quarter slightly missed analysts' consensus estimates, and the company narrowed its full-year adjusted earnings guidance.

Infosys tumbled 5.6% after the consulting company narrowly missed Wall Street's estimates for its earnings per share in the fiscal second quarter and trimmed its revenue guidance for fiscal 2027.

Some hard-hit tech names were rising, but not enough to make a dent in yesterday's selling. Shares of Micron, Intel, and Sandisk, were all higher, while CoreWeave fell 1.4%.

Meta Platforms was down 0.6% after a 7% post-earnings drop Thursday.

SK Hynix was outperforming, though, gaining 4.2% after the company decided to scrap the planned U.S. IPO of its Solidigm memory-chip unit.

Western Digital fell 1.9% even after the company outlined an optimistic fiscal second-quarter outlook and reported widening profits. Fears about a faltering AI trade likely concerned investors.

SLB advanced 6.6%. The company reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings as its push into the AI data center market gained momentum. Management attributed SLB's strong earnings to a "gradual recovery" in the Middle East.

Write to Callum Keown at callum.keown@dowjones.com and Mariapaula Gonzalez at mariapaula.gonzalez@barrons.com

data.title: DoE authorizes 400K-barrel emergency SPR release for Phillips 66 Lake Charles refinery
data.description:
The U.S. Department of Energy said Friday it authorized an emergency release of up to 400K barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption affecting Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery in Louisiana.

"The supply will help offset temporary disruptions affecting crude oil deliveries to the refinery and support continued production of transportation fuels serving Louisiana and surrounding markets," the DoE said, without specifying the nature of the disruption at the 264K bbl/day refinery.

Phillips 66 confirmed it will receive crude from the SPR but did not comment on refinery operations or commercial activity except to say that "we do not anticipate impacts to Lake Charles ⁠operations."

Like most of the recent program of releases from the reserve, the DoE said it authorized release as an exchange, meaning Phillips 66 must return the same amount of oil it receives, along with additional barrels as a premium for the loan.

DoE data this week showed supplies in the reserve now total 282.7M barrels, its lowest level since October 1982, following drawdowns during the U.S.-Iran war and, earlier, Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

data.title: Top News Today:  Stocks Fall as Oil Climbs on Iran War Escalation Bets
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

STOCKS: Stocks fell as rising oil prices weighed on sentiment.

TREASURYS: Treasury yields rose as inflation concerns resurfaced ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting next week.

FOREX: The U.S. dollar strengthened ahead of the Fed meeting.

COMMODITIES: Oil futures rose by more than 3% in New York, blowing past the psychologically significant $100-a-barrel level, due to reports that the U.S. and Israel were weighing more attacks on Iran.

HEADLINES

American Express to Cut 3,500 Jobs

American Express is cutting 5% of its global workforce in an attempt

to put a cap on rising costs.

That reduction amounts to about 3,500 jobs, the company said Friday.

Chief Executive Stephen Squeri said the job reductions were part of a

plan to streamline the organization and invest in business priorities.

"We have got good momentum, but to accelerate innovation and win over

the next few years, we needed to become a more agile and efficient

organization," Squeri said in a conference call with analysts.

Consumer Sentiment Declined Slightly in October

Consumer sentiment ticked slightly lower in October, hovering near

record-low levels, according to the end-of-month reading from the

University of Michigan's survey.

The survey's headline index came in at 48, versus 46.3 in the

preliminary October reading and down from 48.1 in September. It is the

final reading from the survey before November's midterm elections, with

voter frustration about the economy at the center of many campaigns.

Consumers' inflation expectations over both the near term and the long

term moved slightly higher.

SK Hynix Pauses IPO of Memory-Chip Unit as AI Valuation Fears Mount

SEOUL-SK Hynix has scrapped plans for a major U.S. public offering of

its flash-memory subsidiary Solidigm, highlighting deepening investor

caution toward artificial-intelligence valuations despite robust demand

for AI-related hardware.

The memory-chip maker, a key partner to Nvidia, said Friday that

market conditions and broader share-price trends drove the decision, and

that the move doesn't reflect any change in growth prospects for

Solidigm, which was formed after SK Hynix's acquisition of Intel's NAND

flash-memory business.

The Solidigm IPO would have raised funds for a new production facility

in the U.S. to meet rising demand, SK Hynix said.

Trump Expected to Remove Some Tariffs on Canada in Bid to Help Susan

Collins

The U.S. is expected to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian products

in a bid to help Sen. Susan Collins of Maine and other Republicans in the

upcoming midterm elections, according to people familiar with the

upcoming action.

The proclamation altering the tariffs, which could come as early as

Friday, will likely remove 50% tariffs on products used in agriculture,

according to the people, who emphasized that the scope and timing of the

action could change. The tariff reductions could be balanced out by

raising levies on other Canadian goods.

After The Wall Street Journal reported the expected action, Collins

issued a statement praising the Trump administration's move and further

detailing nine categories of tariff exemptions. They include certain

agricultural machinery, refrigeration equipment, packaging products and

other goods used in food production.

Bombardier to Invest $270 Million in U.S. Expansion as Trump Softens

Stance

Bombardier plans to invest $270 million to expand its American

infrastructure footprint and hire 800 U.S. workers, days after President

Trump appeared to soften his rhetoric against the Montreal-based

business-jet maker.

The expansion includes a significant step-up in operations in Texas,

opening a new service center in Indiana, building a learning hub in

Kansas, as well as launching additional infrastructure projects in

Connecticut.

In a Truth Social post at 11:41 P.M. Thursday, hours before

Bombardier's official announcement, Trump praised Bombardier's plans,

stating "Bombardier is investing 270 MILLION DOLLARS, creating THOUSANDS

of American Jobs in Kansas, Texas, and Indiana."

Booz Allen Expects Growth to Accelerate as Civil Business Pressures Ease

Booz Allen Hamilton expects growth to accelerate in the second half of

its fiscal year, driven by continued demand for national-security

technologies and easing pressure in its civil business.

The trends gave the company confidence to raise its full-year earnings

outlook after reporting a higher profit in the latest quarter, even as

revenue declined due to continued weakness in its civil and commercial

business.

Booz Allen is currently operating in a split market, Chief Operating

Officer Kristine Martin Anderson said Friday on a call with analysts.

Rogers Communications Profit Drops on Comparison, Revenue Rises

Rogers Communications reported a decline in third-quarter profit due

to a large prior-year accounting gain tied to its sports assets

acquisition, while adjusted profit topped expectations on higher revenue.

The Canadian telecom company on Friday posted net income of 495

million Canadian dollars ($353.3 million), or C$0.88 a share, down from

C$5.77 billion, or C$10.54 a share, in the comparable quarter a year ago.

In the same period last year, Rogers booked a one-time, noncash paper

gain of C$5 billion when it revalued its existing stake in Maple Leaf

Sports & Entertainment, the parent company of the Toronto Maple Leafs and

Toronto Raptors, as part of its acquisition of Bell's ownership stake.

Archer to Launch Air Taxis in Texas

Archer Aviation plans to launch air taxi networks in three Texas

cities.

The electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft are slated to be

used for air-taxi services in Austin, Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth

area, the aircraft company said Friday.

Archer still requires approval from the Federal Aviation

Administration for its air taxi aircraft Midnight. It is in the final

stages of that regulatory process.

TALKING POINT Brokerage Firms Want to Yank Away Your Investor Protections

Should investors be protected from financial advisers, or should it be the other way around?

Regulators may soon decide whether an unlevel playing field should be tilted even more steeply against the little guy.

For years, arbitration has been the primary way individual investors can seek to recover losses caused by a broker or financial adviser. Investors usually don't prevail. At the largest securities-arbitration forum, run by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, which oversees the brokerage business, investors fail to win any damage awards in about three out of four cases that don't close in a settlement.

This March, Finra requested public comment on "modernizing" its arbitration rules. Outside analysts and attorneys expect proposed changes soon, perhaps by year-end.

Among the questions the regulator sought comment on: whether large or complex cases should go to arbitration forums not administered by Finra; whether punitive damages should be limited or precluded; and whether Finra's arbitration panels should include at least one member from the securities industry.

In early 2025, a Finra arbitration panel stunned the securities industry by ordering a unit of Stifel, the St. Louis-based brokerage and investment firm, to pay approximately $132 million, including punitive damages, to investors who claim to have been defrauded by a former Stifel financial adviser.

  • Jason Zweig, The Wall Street Journal

data.title: Dollar Tree, Dollar General Stocks Slide as Their Core Shoppers Get Squeezed — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Anita Hamilton

Shopper fatigue over rising prices might seem like a good thing for discount stores as more people hunt for bargains. But falling shares of Dollar Tree and Dollar General stores show the pressure on their core consumers.

The discounters' stocks both fell more than 6% Friday, before paring some of those losses by late afternoon. The declines placed them among the worst performers in the S&P 500 for the day. It's not just a one-day slump either: both stocks are roughly flat for the year.

Investors are "having concerns around the health of the consumer and rising oil costs after trading heavily into the retail sector yesterday, as higher oil prices can lead to higher inflation," Morningstar's Brett Husslein told Barron's. "We think investors were seeking a safe-haven that is reasonably insulated from AI-related themes yesterday and are now giving up those gains they saw the prior trading day."

While high prices can motivate more affluent shoppers to hunt for deals wherever they can find them, the chains' core consumers are being forced to pick and choose. Overall inflation combined with high fuel prices — oil futures are trading at five-month highs, while gas prices are up more than 40% since the Iran war started — hits lower-income shoppers harder because they have less discretionary income.

"That is forcing consumers, especially at the lower end of the income distribution, to deploy their purchasing power more consciously," PwC economists wrote in a recent report. "Consumers are still spending, but they are increasingly selective about where they spend and what they get in return," the report added.

While Dollar General's sales come mostly from consumables like shampoo and snacks, 18% come from more discretionary items like holiday decorations, picture frames and small appliances. By comparison, Dollar Tree gets just under half its revenue from consumables.

The worry is that the discounters' core shoppers will be forced to scale back on those discretionary purchases. Fewer than 40% of analysts covering either stock rate it Buy or Overweight.
